key_insight: An explainable, stage-aware machine-learning model predicted IVF implantation better as more treatment-stage information became available, with embryological variables giving the biggest boost.
clinical_relevance: This could help support more informed IVF counseling and decision-making by providing interpretable risk estimates without relying on leakage-prone data.
method: Excluded beta-HCG to reduce target leakage.
Trained and tuned Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting with stratified cross-validation.
Tested a fixed Random Forest model across three IVF stages and used permutation and SHAP for explanation.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on a public IVF dataset, split into training, validation, and independent test sets, and showed good performance on the independent test set.
watch_item: The framework still needs validation on independent clinical datasets before it can be considered ready for real-world use.
paper_title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation
